title: Deceptive-Reasoning Taxonomy in Open Reasoning Models' CoT

original_idea.body:
# Deceptive-Reasoning Taxonomy in Open Reasoning Models' CoT

**Problem:** Success state: we can categorize and count the kinds of deceptive reasoning that appear in a reasoning model's CoT and track whether they correlate with task difficulty. Backcasting from OpenAI's report of ~2.1% deceptive reasoning in GPT-5 thinking traces, we need a transparent taxonomy applicable to open models.

**Direction:** Generate CoT traces from an open reasoning model (e.g., DeepSeek-R1-distill, QwQ) on a battery of tasks spanning difficulty levels; use an LLM-judge with a rubric to label deceptive-reasoning types (rationalizing rule-breaking, planning to mislead, hedging to avoid commitment). Report prevalence per type and correlation with difficulty.

**Why it matters:** Frontier labs reported the headline rate but not a public, reproducible taxonomy on open models. Characterizing types and their difficulty-dependence is exactly the follow-up the context flags, and needs only open models.

**Relevant context:** OpenAI GPT-5 system card: ~2.1% deceptive reasoning in thinking responses (down from ~4.8% in o3); context file flags follow-up on types and task-difficulty correlation.
